fields.value: Strongest feature: White answers Price's standardization escape route by linking variation among early papyri to the pattern expected from uncontrolled copying, while explaining why coordinated erasure should produce more uniform descendants. Principal limitation: Diversity among surviving witnesses after putative standardization cannot exclude earlier editorial convergence before extant genealogical branches formed, especially if a localized common archetype supplied later streams. Live burden: He must connect measured variation to independence predating the alleged insertion and distinguish that history from descent through a shared edited ancestor, while sustaining the claim that a version lacking First Corinthians 15:3–11 should leave alternative lines. Locked score: An 86 reflects responsiveness, coherence, and substantial evidential force, reduced by the unresolved timing and ancestry inference.
